steps.label: Homework: Sensors, Analogue and Digital
steps.content:
Homework

Sensors, Analogue and Digital

Year 10

  • Part 1: learn. On each slide, predict by picking an answer, then read why.
  • Part 2: a test drill at the end. It saves your progress.
  • About one hour. Write your notes when a slide asks.
Think → Pair → ShareA shop door opens by itself when you walk up to it. How do you think the door knows you are there?Show the answer

Something in the door system measures what is in front of it. You will find out what it is called, and how it works.

steps.label: What Is a Sensor?
steps.content:
What Is a Sensor?

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A phone screen gets brighter when you go out into the sun.
  • Nobody pressed a button. A small part in the phone measured the light.

items.prompt: Predict: what does that small part do?
options: It makes light for the screen
It measures the light and sends the reading to the phone
It stores photos taken in the sun
items.explain: It measures something in the world around it (here, light) and sends the reading to the computer in the phone. A part that does this is called a sensor. A sensor is an input device: it sends data into the computer.

steps.label: Why Use a Sensor?
steps.content:
Why Use a Sensor?

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A greenhouse must stay warm all day and all night.
  • A sensor can measure the temperature every second.

items.prompt: Predict: why use a sensor and not a person checking a thermometer?
options: A sensor never needs any power at all
A sensor takes readings all the time, day and night
A person cannot read a thermometer
items.explain: A sensor never gets tired and never forgets. It can take a reading every second, all day and all night, and it is more accurate. A person cannot check that often.

steps.label: Common Sensors (1 of 2)
steps.content:
Common Sensors (1 of 2)

What to do: read the table, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

SensorWhat it measures
Temperaturehow hot or cold it is
Lighthow bright it is
Moisturehow wet the soil is
Humidityhow much water vapour is in the air
pHhow acidic or alkaline it is
Pressurehow hard something presses on it
Gashow much of a gas there is, such as carbon dioxide

items.prompt: Predict: a farmer wants to know when the soil in a field is too dry. Which sensor fits best?
items.explain: Moisture. A moisture sensor measures water in the soil. Humidity is water vapour in the air, not in the soil.

steps.label: Common Sensors (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Common Sensors (2 of 2)

What to do: read the table, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

SensorWhat it measures
Acousticsound: how loud it is
Accelerometerspeeding up, slowing down and tilting
Flowhow much liquid or gas flows through a pipe
Levelhow high a liquid is in a tank
Infra-redinfra-red light, such as body heat, or a beam being broken
Magnetic fielda magnetic field, such as a magnet near it
Proximityhow close an object is

items.prompt: Predict: a phone turns the picture round when you turn the phone on its side. Which sensor fits best?
items.explain: Accelerometer. It measures movement and tilting, so the phone knows it has been turned. Proximity measures how close something is.

steps.label: Your Notes: Sensors
steps.content:
Your Notes: Sensors

What to do: open your notes (the notepad button at the top) and write each note in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea.

Note in your notes: in your own words, say what a sensor is.Check my note

A model note: A sensor is an input device. It measures something in the world around it, such as temperature or light, and sends the reading to a computer.

Note in your notes: explain WHY a system uses a sensor and not a person.Check my note

A model note: A sensor takes readings all the time, day and night, and is more accurate. A person gets tired and cannot check that often.

steps.label: Readings That Change Smoothly
steps.content:
Readings That Change Smoothly

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A room warms up from 21 °C to 22 °C.
  • On the way, it is 21.3 °C, then 21.34 °C, then 21.341 °C ...

items.prompt: Predict: how many different temperatures are there between 21 and 22?
items.explain: There is no limit. The temperature changes smoothly and can be any value, with no gaps. Data like this is called analogue data. Temperature, sound and light in the real world are analogue.

steps.label: Data Inside a Computer
steps.content:
Data Inside a Computer

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A computer stores everything in binary: 1s and 0s.
  • A register holds a fixed number of bits, such as 8.

items.prompt: Predict: 8 bits can hold 256 different patterns. Can 8 bits hold every temperature between 21 and 22?
options: Yes, if the bits are big
items.explain: No. Binary has separate steps with gaps between them, so it can only hold some values. Data stored as separate values in binary is called digital data.

steps.label: Compare: Analogue or Digital?
steps.content:
Compare: Analogue or Digital?

What to do: compare the two boxes, then pick a prediction for each question. The reason appears under each one.

Analogue
Changes smoothly.
Any value, no gaps.
Digital
Separate values, in steps.
Stored in binary.

items.prompt: The sound of your voice moving through the air. Which is it?
items.explain: Analogue. The air pressure changes smoothly, with no gaps.

items.prompt: The number 01101001 stored in a register. Which is it?
items.explain: Digital. It is binary: separate values with nothing in between.

steps.label: Why the Microprocessor Needs Digital
steps.content:
Why the Microprocessor Needs Digital

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A microprocessor is a small CPU built into a device, such as a washing machine.
  • Like every CPU, it only works with binary.

items.prompt: Predict: a temperature sensor gives an analogue reading. Can the microprocessor process it as it is?
options: Yes, a CPU can use any data
No: it must be turned into binary first
items.explain: No. A CPU or microprocessor can only process digital (binary) data. An analogue reading has no separate values, so it must be changed into binary first.

steps.label: Sensor In: The ADC
steps.content:
Sensor In: The ADC

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • The sensor gives analogue data.
  • The microprocessor needs digital data.

items.prompt: Predict: what must sit between the sensor and the microprocessor?
options: Something that turns analogue into digital
Something that turns digital into analogue
items.explain: Something that turns analogue into digital. It is called an analogue to digital converter (ADC). The ADC measures the reading and gives a binary number for it.

steps.label: Output: The DAC
steps.content:
Output: The DAC

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A microprocessor sends music to a speaker. The music is stored as binary.
  • A speaker makes sound by moving smoothly in and out.

items.prompt: Predict: what must sit between the microprocessor and the speaker?
options: Something that turns analogue into digital
Something that turns digital into analogue
Another sensor, to hear the music
items.explain: Something that turns digital into analogue. It is called a digital to analogue converter (DAC). A motor that needs a smooth signal to change its speed can need a DAC too.

steps.label: Compare: ADC or DAC?
steps.content:
Compare: ADC or DAC?

What to do: pick a prediction for each question. Ask: which way is the data going? The reason appears under each one.

ADC
Analogue in, digital out.
Sensor to microprocessor.
DAC
Digital in, analogue out.
Microprocessor to speaker or motor.

items.prompt: A microphone records your voice into a computer. Which converter is needed?
items.explain: ADC. Your voice is analogue and goes into the computer, which needs digital.

items.prompt: A computer plays a video with sound through headphones. Which converter is needed?
items.explain: DAC. The sound is stored as digital and must come out as analogue.

steps.label: Your Notes: ADC and DAC
steps.content:
Your Notes: ADC and DAC

What to do: open your notes (the notepad button at the top) and write each note in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea.

Note in your notes: explain WHY a sensor reading must go through an ADC.Check my note

A model note: The sensor gives analogue data. The microprocessor can only process digital (binary) data, so the ADC turns analogue into digital.

Note in your notes: explain WHY a speaker needs a DAC.Check my note

A model note: The sound is stored as digital data. The speaker moves smoothly, so it needs analogue. The DAC turns digital into analogue.

steps.label: Using Sensor Data: Compare
steps.content:
Using Sensor Data: Compare

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A greenhouse has a temperature sensor, a microprocessor and a heater.
  • The microprocessor stores the value 20 °C.

items.prompt: Predict: the sensor reads 17 °C. The ADC turns it into binary. What does the microprocessor do with it?
options: Compares it with the stored value 20
Stores it and does nothing else
Sends it back to the sensor
items.explain: It compares the reading with the stored value. 17 is less than 20, so the greenhouse is too cold.

steps.label: Using Sensor Data: Act
steps.content:
Using Sensor Data: Act

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A greenhouse has a temperature sensor, a microprocessor and a heater.
  • The microprocessor stores the value 20 °C.

items.prompt: Predict: 17 is less than 20. What does the microprocessor do next?
options: Waits for a person to switch on the heater
Sends a signal to switch the heater on
items.explain: It sends a signal to switch the heater on. A device that the microprocessor switches on or off to make something happen is called an actuator. A motor, a pump and a valve are actuators too.

steps.label: Using Sensor Data: Repeat
steps.content:
Using Sensor Data: Repeat

What to do: read the slide, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • A greenhouse has a temperature sensor, a microprocessor and a heater.
  • The microprocessor stores the value 20 °C.

items.prompt: Predict: the heater is on. What does the system do next?
options: Turns the sensor off to save power
Takes a new reading and checks again
items.explain: It takes a new reading and checks again, over and over. When the reading reaches 20, the heater is switched off. The steps are: read, convert (ADC), compare, act, repeat.

steps.label: Check: The Steps in Order
steps.content:
Check: The Steps in Order

What to do: pick the best order. Done when it is answered.

items.prompt: A water tank fills by itself. A level sensor is used. Which order is right?
items.explain: Read the level, convert it with the ADC, compare it with the stored level, act (switch the pump on or off), then repeat. You cannot compare a reading before it is read and converted.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Automatic Tap
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Automatic Tap

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, November 2022, Question 2(a). What to do: type your answer, then press Submit answer. Use the steps: read, convert, compare, act, repeat.

items.prompt: An automated water tap system uses a sensor and a microprocessor to operate. Water flows from the tap when a person's hands are placed underneath the tap. Water stops flowing when the person's hands are removed from underneath the tap. Explain how the water tap system uses a sensor and a microprocessor to operate.
scheme: Data is converted from analogue to digital (using ADC)
Data is compared to stored/set value(s)
If data is inside range/outside range/greater than/less than, signal is sent to turn water tap on
If data is outside range/inside range/less than/greater than, tap remains off // signal is sent to turn water tap off
Actuator is used to turn the tap off/on
items.guidance: Six from the points, one mark each.
items.modelAnswer: A proximity sensor sends data to the microprocessor. An ADC converts it to digital. It is compared with a stored value. If hands are near, a signal makes an actuator turn the tap on, otherwise off. This repeats continuously.
